endowment_summary: Began golf at age 5, attracted media attention by 7, won a professional tour event at 14, and became the youngest LPGA Tour winner at 15 and youngest world No. 1 at 17. Prodigy-level ability with natural swing and extraordinary composure from a very young age.
inherited_summary: Korean immigrant family that moved to New Zealand when she was 4-6, partly to further her golf development. Parents were not golfers but were highly supportive; middle-class family in Auckland. No domain overlap or significant wealth.
ecosystem_summary: Coached by Guy Wilson at Pupuke Golf Club from age 5 for nearly a decade, providing sustained dedicated mentorship. New Zealand golf environment offered accessible facilities and competitive opportunities for a young prodigy.

endowment_summary: Started playing football at SSV Siegburg at age 9, selected for Kreis and Mittelrhein regional teams at 11, and played for the German school team at Wembley at 12. Above-average talent but not a prodigy.
inherited_summary: Youngest of eight children in a strict Catholic, modest family in Siegburg. Father was a war-wounded city treasury clerk; family affected by WWII losses including two brothers killed. Simple working-class upbringing.
ecosystem_summary: SSV Siegburg youth system, mentored by Mittelrhein Verband trainer Karl-Heinz Heddergott, then 1. FC Köln pipeline. Joined Köln at 19 and won the inaugural Bundesliga title, benefiting from one of Germany's elite club systems.

endowment_summary: Attended a specialist sports school in Plovdiv, introduced to high jump at 12-13, jumped 166cm in 6th grade and 190cm by 10th grade. Set a world record of 2.09m at 22 that stood for 37 years. Exceptional athletic talent.
inherited_summary: Parents divorced when she was 4; raised by her mother with help from grandparents on a single salary and pensions. Modest family with no athletic background or wealth.
ecosystem_summary: Specialist sports school in Plovdiv, Bulgarian state athletics system, and coach Nikolay Petrov (who became her husband) provided sustained elite-level training. The Bulgarian athletics pipeline was among the world's best for high jump.

endowment_summary: Champion of Zlatoust in skiing by 3rd grade, set national speed skating records at 17, qualified for the Soviet team at 19. Exceptional athletic versatility across skiing, athletics, and speed skating.
inherited_summary: Working-class family in Zlatoust, Soviet Union. Father was deputy director of an abrasive plant, mother was a housewife raising five children. Modest upbringing with no athletic family background.
ecosystem_summary: Soviet state sports system through Burevestnik Chelyabinsk and later Lokomotiv Moscow clubs. Coaches Boris Mishin (athletics/skiing) and Boris Lukin (skating) provided early guidance. The Soviet institutional pipeline was world-class for speed skating.

endowment_summary: Learned to skate on frozen streams in Poprad with older brother Juraj. Joined VSŽ Košice's First Division team at 18 and was considered one of the top shooters by his second season. Above-average talent accelerated by his brother.
inherited_summary: Father was a bus driver who died in 1982 when Peter was 14, creating significant hardship. Mother worked on a cooperative farm. Slovak-Polish working-class family that had moved from Soviet Ukraine to Czechoslovakia when Peter was 3.
ecosystem_summary: Brother Juraj was already playing at Košice and facilitated Peter's transfer. HK Poprad and VSŽ Košice provided the Czechoslovak First Division pipeline. Washington Capitals scout Jack Button spotted him, leading to his NHL career.

endowment_summary: Started fencing at 13 at the Marymont club in Warsaw, won the junior world championship in Genoa at 20, and Olympic team foil gold at 23. Above-average talent developed through systematic training.
inherited_summary: Born in Warsaw to Tadeusz and Janina. No notable family wealth or fencing background documented. Ordinary Polish family.
ecosystem_summary: Marymont Warsaw fencing club under coaches Władysław Kurpiewski and Władysław Dobrowolski, then AZS-AWF Warsaw and Legia Warsaw. The Polish fencing pipeline was among the world's strongest, providing elite coaching and competitive structure.

endowment_summary: Started racing production cars at 23 and progressed to Formula Junior at 25. Won his first three F1 races including the French Grand Prix on debut at 26. Talented but not a prodigy; his career was enabled more by opportunity than exceptional early ability.
inherited_summary: Born into a wealthy Milanese industrialist family; his father and grandfather were wealthy industrialists who established a successful foundry. Family wealth enabled his motorsport career from his early twenties, including purchasing racing cars.
ecosystem_summary: FISA (Italian motorsport federation) selected him to drive a privateer Ferrari 156, providing a trajectory-changing opportunity. Milanese tuner/engineer Angelo Dagrada was a key mentor who designed his Formula Junior car. The Italian motorsport network provided critical access.

endowment_summary: Environmental activist from childhood, destroying animal traps at age 9. Strong personal drive and commitment to animal protection from a very young age, though not a traditional cognitive prodigy.
inherited_summary: Mother died when he was 13, after which he had a difficult relationship with his father. Eldest of seven children. Family instability and early loss shaped his independent path.
ecosystem_summary: Gained maritime experience through the Canadian Coast Guard and merchant marine. Immersed himself in Vancouver's environmental protest scene in the early 1970s, co-founding Greenpeace at 22 with a group of like-minded activists in a key frontier for the environmental movement.

endowment_summary: Learned chess at home from his father, a well-known Lviv chess player. Won the European Junior Championship at 21, earned GM title at 24. Strong creative and aggressive playing style recognized from early on.
inherited_summary: Father Mikhailo Romanishin was a prominent pre-war Lviv chess player who co-founded the Lviv chess club after WWII. Chess was a family domain — father taught all three sons, playing hundreds of games with Oleg.
ecosystem_summary: Trained at the famous Lviv 'Kart school' under Viktor Kart alongside future GMs Beliavsky and Mikhalchishin. Later mentored by ex-world champion Mikhail Tal. The Soviet chess pipeline provided institutional support and intense peer competition — a once-in-a-generation chess environment.

endowment_summary: Started modern pentathlon at 17, switched to épée fencing at 22, and reached the world championship podium by 25. Good all-around athletic ability but a relatively late developer in fencing.
inherited_summary: Father was active in the Hungarian fencing federation and clubs, directing István into the sport at age 16. Family had direct domain involvement in fencing administration.
ecosystem_summary: Benefited from Hungary's world-dominant fencing program, joining top clubs (Vasas, then OSC Budapest) and rising through the national team pipeline. The Hungarian fencing system was one of the world's best.

endowment_summary: Showed climbing talent in local races but turned professional late at around 24-27, working as a watchmaker and electrician while racing. Self-trained climber with evident natural ability but limited early development.
inherited_summary: Modest family in Ávila with no cycling tradition. Father was an army driver/chauffeur who gave him his first bike. Working-class background with no domain connections.
ecosystem_summary: Former Tour winner Federico Bahamontes noticed his climbing talent at the 1968 Tour de l'Avenir and helped him secure a professional contract. Spanish cycling culture provided context, but he lacked elite early access or coaching.

endowment_summary: Politically active from his teens, attended art school before dropping out for financial reasons. Charismatic and brave but not a traditional cognitive prodigy; his abilities were in leadership and guerrilla warfare.
inherited_summary: Born into a working-class Havana family of Spanish anarchist immigrants. Father was a tailor with intermittent work, causing frequent moves. Poverty and political repression shaped his early life.
ecosystem_summary: Father's anarchist political activism exposed him to left-wing ideas early. Joined Castro's 26th of July Movement and partnered with Che Guevara in guerrilla warfare. His ecosystem was forged through adversity rather than elite institutions.

endowment_summary: Taught himself programming at 14-15 from a textbook, spending hours after school coding on Atari 800s. Worked at a game company at 16 and shipped a commercial game by 21. Self-taught with exceptional curiosity and drive.
inherited_summary: Mother worked for the Judge Advocate General's Corps, providing a middle-class suburban upbringing in Alexandria, Virginia. Mother's office connections introduced him to D&D at 14, shaping his game design sensibility.
ecosystem_summary: High school acquired Atari 800 computers, and his sister's college programming textbook was available at home. A friend's connection got him a job at CYBRON at 16. Access to computers was timely but not exceptional for the era.

endowment_summary: Started fencing at 10, became Romanian national champion after just six months of training, left home at 13 to train at the Olympic Center in Craiova. Won World Cadet Championship at 16-17 and World Junior Championship at 17-18. Exceptional early talent.
inherited_summary: Born in the Rahova district of Bucharest, second of two children. Parents pushed her toward sport but had no fencing background or notable wealth. Elder brother played football at CSA Steaua and introduced her to the fencing hall.
ecosystem_summary: CSS 3 Steaua Bucharest under coach Radu Szilaghy, then the Olympic Center in Craiova under Dan Podeanu and Cornel Milan. Romania's elite fencing pipeline provided centralized training and competitive structure from a young age.

endowment_summary: Competed at ski jumping's top level from age 19, won four Austrian national titles, and set a hill record at Holmenkollen in 1959. Solid talent developed in a strong ski jumping culture.
inherited_summary: Born in Mariazell, Styria, in the heart of Austrian ski jumping country. Brother Alois was also an Olympic ski jumper. Family was deeply connected to the local skiing community.
ecosystem_summary: Mariazell's alpine terrain and ski jumping tradition provided natural early immersion. The Austrian national team and Four Hills Tournament ecosystem offered elite competitive opportunities. Brother Alois provided a sibling training partner.

endowment_summary: Entered the University of Tehran Faculty of Law at 17, completed her law degree in just 3.5 years, became one of Iran's first female judges at 21-22, and earned a PhD at 23-24. Exceptional academic ability and drive.
inherited_summary: Father was Mohammad Ali Ebadi, one of Iran's first commercial law professors and a chief notary public. Academic family with deep legal domain expertise. Father's book 'Commercial Law' was later revised by Shirin herself.
ecosystem_summary: University of Tehran Faculty of Law provided the institutional pathway. Her father's legal expertise and academic network shaped her early trajectory. The cultural context of 1960s Iran created both opportunity and barriers for women in law.

endowment_summary: Playing golf by age 4 at Stackstown GC, reached scratch handicap by 15, represented Ireland 114 times and played in three Walker Cups before turning professional at 24. Strong talent developed through constant early play.
inherited_summary: Youngest of five sons in a Dublin family. Father Paddy was a Garda who played golf to a five handicap and co-founded Stackstown Golf Club. Four older brothers all played golf, creating a competitive family golf environment.
ecosystem_summary: Stackstown GC, co-founded by his father, was his childhood playground where he played 45 holes a day. Irish amateur golf pipeline and Walker Cup experience provided elite competitive development. School peer Paul McGinley also became a Ryder Cup captain.

endowment_summary: Started playing table tennis at 7, won the European Youth Cadet Championship at 14, and moved to Borussia Düsseldorf at 16 to train professionally. Prodigy-level talent identified early by the Danish system.
inherited_summary: Mother was Danish and father was a London football player, providing a sports-oriented family background. Modest family in Faxe, Denmark.
ecosystem_summary: Spotted at 14 winning the European Youth Cadet Championship. Moved to Borussia Düsseldorf at 16, one of Europe's top table tennis programs. Danish national team and coach Mikael Andersson provided systematic development.

endowment_summary: Debuted in the Czech extraliga at 18 and won the Czechoslovak league with Jihlava at 20. Career nearly stalled at 21 when he was without a team and worked as an electrician. Late bloomer who needed a second chance.
inherited_summary: No family advantages or wealth documented. Ordinary Czech family background. His career adversity (working as an electrician) suggests modest means.
ecosystem_summary: Czech hockey system through HC Zlín and Jihlava. Coach Horst Valášek brought him to Vsetín, where he won multiple Czech Extraliga titles. The Vsetín dynasty provided the platform for his late development into a world-class goaltender.

endowment_summary: Made stage debut at age 3 in his father's play. Studied at universities in Basel, Zurich, and Munich. Immersed in theatre from birth, though his early ability was more about exposure than prodigy-level talent.
inherited_summary: Mother was an actress who ran an acting school. Father was a Swiss playwright, novelist, and pharmacy owner. Elder sister Maria Schell became an international film star. Wealthy, cultured Viennese theatrical family that fled to Switzerland in 1938.
ecosystem_summary: Grew up surrounded by performance and literature in Vienna and Zürich. Sister Maria's international film career provided Hollywood connections that facilitated his later entry into international cinema. Swiss cultural environment after fleeing the Anschluss.

endowment_summary: Dropped out of high school at 16, signed with Elite Modeling Agency, and took acting classes. Developed adaptability from constant relocations (30+ moves by age 14) but showed no traditional prodigy-level ability.
inherited_summary: Biological father deserted before her birth. Stepfather Dan Guynes was an alcoholic who frequently changed jobs. Mother was an alcoholic with a long arrest record. Turbulent, unstable childhood with 30+ relocations and severe family dysfunction.
ecosystem_summary: Moved to Los Angeles as a teenager, signed with Elite Modeling Agency, and secured early roles through a connection at 20th Century Fox. The Brat Pack peer group of the 1980s provided a career-accelerating social network.

endowment_summary: Played soccer through Meisei High School and Kansai University before joining Yanmar Diesel in 1968. Selected for the Japan national team the same year. Above-average ability but no documented exceptional early talent.
inherited_summary: Born in Osaka. No family background, wealth, or domain connections documented.
ecosystem_summary: Meisei High School and Kansai University provided the educational-sports pipeline. Yanmar Diesel was a company team in the Japan Soccer League. The 1968 Mexico City Olympics provided the international platform for his bronze medal.

endowment_summary: Showed climbing talent at the 1968 Tour de l'Avenir, turned pro in 1969, and won the Tour de France mountains classification and finished 3rd overall at 24. Natural climbing ability but relatively late professional development.
inherited_summary: Grew up in Erpe-Mere, Belgium. Father was a cycling fan who encouraged him and watched the Tour de France with him on television. Modest family in Belgian cycling culture.
ecosystem_summary: Former Tour winner Federico Bahamontes noticed his climbing talent at the Tour de l'Avenir and facilitated his professional contract. Belgian cycling culture and the European professional cycling circuit provided the competitive ecosystem.

endowment_summary: Switched from ice hockey to handball at 16, making an immediate impact with 20 goals in his first two Polish premier league matches. Exceptional scoring ability and physical coordination evident from the start.
inherited_summary: Born in Międzylesie, moved to Opole at 11. Sister was a handball player who encouraged his switch from ice hockey. No family wealth or domain advantages documented.
ecosystem_summary: Gwardia Opole under coach Edward Hyla, then Śląsk Wrocław's dominant program that won seven consecutive league titles (1972-78). The Polish handball system and the Śląsk 'dream team' provided an elite competitive environment.

endowment_summary: Began violin at 5 through El Sistema, started conducting at 14, appointed music director of the Simón Bolívar Youth Symphony Orchestra at 18, and won the Gustav Mahler Conducting Competition at 23. Prodigy-level conducting ability from a young age.
inherited_summary: Father was a trombonist in a salsa band and mother was a voice teacher. Both parents were professional musicians, providing a musical household and direct domain knowledge from birth.
ecosystem_summary: El Sistema, Venezuela's revolutionary music education program, provided free instruments and instruction from age 5. José Antonio Abreu, El Sistema's founder, became his key mentor. The Simón Bolívar Youth Orchestra was a once-in-a-generation peer environment for orchestral training.

endowment_summary: Started playing basketball at ~13 at FIS outdoor courts in Sarajevo. Won FIBA European U18 silver with Yugoslavia at 19. Good talent but not exceptional; his greater abilities emerged in coaching.
inherited_summary: Father was a Yugoslav People's Army officer and former partisan who was the first post-war commander of Pljevlja. Military family that moved to Sarajevo when Bogdan was 4. Modest but stable upbringing.
ecosystem_summary: Sarajevo basketball environment at FIS courts with peers Uglješa Uzelac and Davorin Popović. Moved to Belgrade to play for OKK Beograd, one of Yugoslavia's top clubs. The Yugoslav basketball system was among the world's best.

endowment_summary: Started playing volleyball at 14 with brother Vladimir under father's guidance. Joined Vojvodina Novi Sad and the Yugoslavian national team at 18, winning Olympic bronze at 22. Solid talent developed in a family volleyball environment.
inherited_summary: Father Miloš Grbić was a Yugoslav national team volleyball player. Older brother Vladimir also became a Volleyball Hall of Famer. Total family immersion in volleyball — father coached, both sons played internationally.
ecosystem_summary: GIK Banat Zrenjanin and Vojvodina Novi Sad provided the club pipeline. Father Miloš was the primary early coach. The Yugoslavian national team and volleyball system provided elite competitive development. Brother Vladimir was a lifelong playing partner.

endowment_summary: Won the Czechoslovak Chess Championship at 19, the youngest player ever to do so. Earned the Grandmaster title at 22. Self-taught through clubs and poring over chess theory. Strong talent developed independently.
inherited_summary: Mother was a nurse. Father was a radio journalist who left Czechoslovakia in 1948 during the Communist takeover and worked for Radio Free Europe in West Germany. Father was absent during Kavalek's childhood, creating family separation.
ecosystem_summary: Prague's strong chess tradition and clubs provided the early development environment. Charles University journalism studies ran parallel to chess. The Czechoslovak chess pipeline and Soviet-bloc competitive structure provided strong opposition and development.

endowment_summary: Joined Barcelona's La Masia academy at 17, relatively late for an elite footballer. Progressed through Barcelona C and B teams before debuting in La Liga at 21. Good talent but not a childhood prodigy; his strengths were determination and physicality.
inherited_summary: Working-class family from the small Catalan town of La Pobla de Segur. Father was a farmer who died in a farming accident in 2006. Parents were skeptical about him becoming a footballer and encouraged him to study.
ecosystem_summary: La Masia, Barcelona's world-renowned youth academy, provided one of football's elite development pipelines. Coach Louis van Gaal promoted him to the first team. The Xavi-Iniesta peer network at La Masia created a once-in-a-generation player development environment.

endowment_summary: Taught himself tightrope walking at 16 and mastered all wire skills within a year, including backward somersaults and unicycle. Expelled from five schools. Exceptional self-directed learning and physical creativity.
inherited_summary: Father was an author and French Army pilot/colonel. Middle-class French family with no connection to performance art. Parents did not understand his desire to become a wandering performer.
ecosystem_summary: Developed his art as a street performer in Paris rather than through formal circus training. Paris's cultural milieu provided inspiration and audience. Self-created his unconventional artistic path without institutional support.

endowment_summary: Inspired by discovering Roman remains at 9 on his uncle's farm. Sailed through six A-levels at his state grammar school and studied archaeology at St John's College, Cambridge, where he was president of the Archaeological Field Club. Exceptional academic ability.
inherited_summary: Widowed mother raised him in bomb-scarred Portsmouth. Uncle's farm in Somerset provided the catalytic childhood experience. Working-class background with no academic family tradition.
ecosystem_summary: Portsmouth Northern Grammar School provided the educational pipeline. St John's College, Cambridge offered elite institutional access. Peer Colin Renfrew (later a fellow eminent archaeologist) was a course mate. Cambridge's archaeology department was world-class.

endowment_summary: Turned professional at 14, the youngest American to do so at the time. Defeated the 20th-ranked local player after just two weeks of training. No. 2 in the US 12-and-under by 12. Strong natural athletic ability and powerful groundstrokes.
inherited_summary: Father Jim Pierce was an ex-Marine with a criminal record who became her coach but was also physically and emotionally abusive, slapping her after losses and making terroristic threats. Family revolved coercively around her tennis. Active disadvantage despite tennis immersion.
ecosystem_summary: Grew up in Florida, a major tennis training hub. After separating from her abusive father, worked with Nick Bollettieri. Country club junior clinic provided initial access. The WTA and French tennis system (through her mother's citizenship) provided competitive pathways.

endowment_summary: Began fencing at 7, won her first national championship at 12, joined the Romanian senior national team at 16, and won the Junior World title at 19. Exceptional early talent developed through intensive early training.
inherited_summary: Hungarian-ethnic family in Brașov, Romania. Elder brother already fenced at CS Tractorul, which introduced her to the sport. No family wealth or fencing background documented.
ecosystem_summary: CS Tractorul Brașov under coaches Petre Dumitrescu, Bogdan Pincovici, and Vlad Șerban provided early development. The Romanian national fencing pipeline and senior team coaches (Stefan Haukler, Tudor Petrus) sustained her 21-year international career.

endowment_summary: Selected for the Chinese national women's volleyball team at 18. Nicknamed the 'Iron Hammer,' she became the star outside hitter leading China to four consecutive international championship titles. Exceptional athletic talent and mental toughness.
inherited_summary: Born in Tianjin in 1960 during widespread famine. Family was very poor — she slept on a wooden plank and had only three sets of clothes. Father was a policeman, mother a hotel manager. Poverty and material scarcity defined her early years.
ecosystem_summary: Chinese state sports system provided intensive training, dedicated coaching, and elite facilities from a young age. Beijing Workers' Stadium amateur sports school was her entry point. The national team's systematic approach enabled rapid rise to international dominance.

endowment_summary: Developed a passion for arts and crafts at Bedales School. Trained at Parnham House under John Makepeace from 1980-82. Founded his furniture company at 23. Good craftsmanship ability but not prodigy-level.
inherited_summary: Son of Princess Margaret and Antony Armstrong-Jones, 1st Earl of Snowdon. Born at Clarence House, educated in the Buckingham Palace schoolroom. British royal family provided immense inherited wealth, status, and access to elite networks and clients.
ecosystem_summary: Bedales School fostered his craft interests. Parnham House under renowned furniture maker John Makepeace provided elite training. Royal family connections (Queen Mother as lifelong supporter, clients like Elton John and Valentino) opened doors that were unavailable to ordinary craftsmen.

endowment_summary: Studied accounting before being discovered at a hair salon at 21. No exceptional early ability or training; her success was based on physical appearance and a chance discovery.
inherited_summary: Raised by her aunts and father in Buenos Aires. Modest family with no fashion or pageant connections. Brother Aldo became her manager after her pageant success.
ecosystem_summary: Discovered at a hair salon by the wife of French designer Jean Cartier, which led to modeling and the Miss World pageant pipeline. The Miss Argentina and Miss World competitions provided the platform for her breakthrough.

endowment_summary: Started skiing at 10-11 at the local Yxbacken hill. Described herself as 'never a super talent, a training product' who relied on intense training and willpower. Above-average ability with exceptional work ethic.
inherited_summary: Sports-oriented family in Norrköping, Sweden. Father was athletic (ran fast), older sister Annika influenced her to start skiing. Middle-class family that supported her athletic development.
ecosystem_summary: Moved to the ski gymnasium in Malung at 16 for specialized alpine racing training. Swedish national team system provided structured development. The ski gymnasium was a key institutional stepping stone despite limited local training conditions in Norrköping.

endowment_summary: Started skating at 5 at Prague's Štvanice Stadium, competed in her first competition at 8, won her first title at 10, made international debut at 13, and won World Championship bronze at 17. Exceptional early talent as a jumper.
inherited_summary: Father was a hotel waiter, mother a kindergarten cook. Family suffered profound tragedy — father (mother's first husband) murdered two of Hana's half-siblings and committed suicide. Deeply troubled family background with severe mental illness.
ecosystem_summary: Štvanice Stadium in Prague provided the training venue. Coach Karel Glogar, who had worked with two-time World champion Ája Vrzáňová, identified her talent. Multiple dedicated coaches (Sadílek, Nováková, Koudelka) and the Czechoslovak skating system sustained her development.

endowment_summary: Started playing hockey at 3 on a backyard rink his father built. Signed with the Chicago Black Hawks as a teenager and became an NHL regular at 22. Good talent with strong size and shooting ability, though not a fast or graceful skater.
inherited_summary: Working-class Italian-Canadian family in Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario. Father worked in the Algoma Steel Mill and built the family's first house for $3,000. Brother Tony also became an NHL Hall of Famer. No wealth or domain connections.
ecosystem_summary: Sault Ste. Marie was a hockey heartland with abundant outdoor rinks. Brother Tony was a lifelong training partner. Chicago Black Hawks organization signed him and provided the junior/minor league pipeline. Centering for Bobby Hull accelerated his development.

endowment_summary: Started modeling at 14, photographed by top Czech fashion photographer Jadran Šetlík by 15, and arrived in Milan by 17. Physical appearance was her primary asset; no exceptional cognitive or creative ability documented.
inherited_summary: Born in Prague, younger sister Eliška also became a model. Middle-class family with no fashion industry connections documented.
ecosystem_summary: Photographer Jadran Šetlík provided early professional exposure at 15. Milan, a European fashion capital, provided geographic proximity to the modeling industry. The Miss Czech Republic pageant pipeline elevated her profile.

endowment_summary: Won his first cycling race at 14, became junior champion of Ireland, and dominated Irish junior and senior racing. Precocious talent with exceptional physical toughness and competitive drive.
inherited_summary: Grew up in poverty on a small 45-acre farm in Curraghduff, County Waterford. Left school at 13 to work on the farm after his father's hospitalization. Became a bricklayer at 16. Active economic disadvantage.
ecosystem_summary: Brother Joe introduced him to cycling through the Carrick Wheelers club. Trainer Tony Ryan pushed him with severe training in the Comeragh Mountains. Jean de Gribaldy, the wealthy Flandria team manager, pursued him to Ireland to sign him professionally.

endowment_summary: Was a member of the Austrian national junior B skiing team before turning to motorsport. Started racing with a Mini Cooper purchased from Niki Lauda in 1969. Good athletic ability and adaptability across sports.
inherited_summary: Parents were pharmacists in Vienna, providing a comfortable middle-class background. However, parents saw motorsport as reckless and refused to support his racing ambitions, creating financial constraints.
ecosystem_summary: Purchased his first racing car from Niki Lauda, a pivotal network connection. Helmut Marko spotted him and invited him to test a Formula Vee car, launching his single-seater career. The Austrian motorsport network and Kaimann team provided competitive opportunities.

endowment_summary: Started attending handball practices with his father at 5, began playing at 9, made his senior debut in the Croatian first division at 14-16, and became the league's top scorer before 18. Exceptional talent recognized from childhood.
inherited_summary: Born into an extraordinary handball family — father was a handball coach, mother played, sister played, uncle coached, and cousins all played. Total family immersion in the sport from birth.
ecosystem_summary: RK Đakovo in the Croatian first division provided early senior-level competition. Coach Lino Cervar recognized his talent and took him under his wing at RK Zagreb in 2006. The Croatian national team system provided the pathway to international success.

endowment_summary: Discovered at 11 by Arthur Ashe during a tennis clinic in Cameroon, impressing the Wimbledon champion with his natural ability. Aced Ashe during their hitting session. Strong athletic talent from a young age.
inherited_summary: Father Zacharie Noah was a professional Cameroonian footballer who won the French Cup with Sedan in 1961. Mother Marie-Claire was a teacher and former captain of France's basketball team. Elite sports family on both sides.
ecosystem_summary: Arthur Ashe's discovery at 11 was trajectory-changing — Ashe recommended him to the French Tennis Federation, which brought him to its training center in Nice in 1971. The FFT pipeline and coach Patrice Hagelauer provided structured elite development.

endowment_summary: Won the 165-pound Amateur Wrestling Championship of Manitoba at 15. Proficient in bagpipes from a young age. First professional wrestling match at 15. Strong physical ability and charisma but no traditional cognitive prodigy traits.
inherited_summary: Father was an RCMP/CN Police officer. Left home as a young teenager after conflicts with his father and expulsion from school. Lived in youth hostels and on gymnasium floors. Active family dysfunction and early independence.
ecosystem_summary: Winnipeg gyms and the prairie wrestling circuit provided early immersion. Trained by Judo Gene LeBell, Leo Garibaldi, Tony Condello, and Stu Hart. The Canadian wrestling circuit offered a grassroots development path, though not an elite institutional pipeline.

endowment_summary: Folk dancing at 6, accepted into Kyiv Choreography School at 10. Youngest contestant at the Vaganova-Prix competition, won second prize, and was invited to the Vaganova Academy's graduating class — the first time a student was allowed to skip two grades. Principal dancer at Mariinsky at 18. Prodigy-level ability with phenomenal physique.
inherited_summary: Mother was a choreographer who took her to folk dancing at 6 and to the Kyiv audition. Father was a serviceman. Mother's dance background provided early direction but no significant wealth or elite connections.
ecosystem_summary: Kyiv Choreography School from age 10 under Valeria Sulegina, then the Vaganova Academy of Russian Ballet (skipping two grades, unprecedented). The Mariinsky Ballet at 17, rehearsed under Olga Moiseeva. These represent the pre-eminent Russian ballet institutional pipeline — a once-in-a-generation training environment.

endowment_summary: Scouted just before her 17th birthday while working at McDonald's. Her androgynous appearance at 6'1" was a striking physical attribute that enabled walking both men's and women's shows at Paris Fashion Week at 19. Physical edge rather than cognitive prodigy.
inherited_summary: Born in Tuzla, Yugoslavia (Bosnia). Fled to Serbia as a refugee during the Bosnian War, then moved to Melbourne as a political refugee in 2000. Mother was university-educated but took cleaning jobs; parents divorced. Poverty and displacement defined her early years.
ecosystem_summary: University High in Melbourne was a liberal, multicultural school that encouraged individuality. Scouted at 17, she quickly reached Paris Fashion Week through Jean-Paul Gaultier and Marc Jacobs. The rising cultural wave around gender fluidity provided perfect timing for her unique look.

endowment_summary: Awarded the top open scholarship to Trinity College, Cambridge in 1954 in chemistry/physics, then read mathematics and architecture. Completed the first-ever PhD in Architecture at Harvard. Cross-disciplinary depth spanning architecture, mathematics, transportation theory, and cognitive studies. Exceptional intellectual ability.
inherited_summary: Born in Vienna to a Catholic father and Jewish mother, both archaeologists (some sources say they worked as German language teachers after fleeing). Family fled the Nazis to England in 1938. Cultured family background but refugee status created displacement.
ecosystem_summary: Dragon School and Oundle School provided elite English education. Trinity College, Cambridge (top open scholarship), then Harvard and MIT. This represents a once-in-a-generation institutional pipeline — the elite British schooling system combined with top American universities at the dawn of modern design theory.

endowment_summary: An ordinary Bolivian Army sergeant with no documented exceptional ability. His historical significance came from a single event — executing Che Guevara — rather than any personal achievement built on early advantages.
inherited_summary: Born to Vicente Terán, a merchant who was 46 when Mario was born, and Candelaria Salazar, who was 45. Ordinary family in Cochabamba with no notable wealth, connections, or domain advantages.
ecosystem_summary: Joined the Bolivian military in 1959 at 17. His unit was trained by US Green Beret and CIA operatives, but this was standard institutional training rather than an exceptional individual ecosystem. No notable peers or mentors documented.

endowment_summary: Discovered a love for art in junior high school. Earned a BA in art (1969-72) and MA in painting (1972) at the University of Iowa. Good creative ability that channeled personal trauma into groundbreaking earth-body art.
inherited_summary: Born to a wealthy, politically prominent Havana family — father was an attorney and nephew of a Cuban president; mother was a chemist and granddaughter of a sugar mill owner. However, exiled at 12 via Operation Pedro Pan, separated from parents, and moved through foster homes and institutions in Iowa. Wealthy origin offset by profound displacement trauma.
ecosystem_summary: University of Iowa's Intermedia program and mentor Hans Breder provided avant-garde artistic training. The feminist art movement of the 1970s and the trauma of exile from Cuba became the raw material for her earth-body artworks. Iowa's landscape shaped her signature Silueta series.
